summary: Border site: 1920s camp, 1930 log cupola now in BC, 1953 US L-4 tower (TrailChick says 1952), last used 1970s; hike-in in Pasayten Wilderness.

facts.design: 1930 log cupola cabin (now in Canada) and 30 ft L-4 timber tower (1953)

staffing.status: no current staffing reported; last used for emergencies in the 1970s

access.note: Hike-in only, in the Pasayten Wilderness. The sources read describe no closure.

visit.trail_note: Firelookout.com gives a 10-mile trail from the Canadian side or 30 miles from the US side through the Pasayten Wilderness. TrailChick calls it a good winter ski-touring spot if the trail is clear of fallen trees.

facts.agency: US Forest Service - Okanogan National Forest

events.note: Camp with a tree platform first established in the 1920s
Log cabin cupola constructed and celebrated as northernmost US lookout; later surveys placed it a few feet inside Canada
Aircraft Warning Service site, July to September 1942
30 ft treated timber L-4 tower built on the US side. TrailChick gives 1952 for this tower
Last used for emergencies in the 1970s

corrections.why: The brief lists only the 1930 cupola. NHLR and firelookout.com both date the L-4 tower to 1953; TrailChick says 1952.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR and firelookout.com both give 1953. TrailChick gives 1952. The record uses 1953 from the two sources that agree and flags TrailChick's year.

notes_for_editor: The brief's record gives 1930 only; the 1953 tower is the main gap. The 1952 vs 1953 tower year is a real source conflict and is flagged, not settled. The 'fire' and current-condition claims rest on 2019 TrailChick photos and undated NHLR and firelookout.com text.
